title: Escape game to learn electronic and robotics
author: Own_Egg_9141
selftext:
Hey! I am building an **escape room-style video game where you learn the basics of electronics, circuits, and robotics by solving puzzles.**

The concept is that you must design small robots, fix in-game puzzles and simple circuits... to escape the rooms. The learning is directly integrated into the rooms. Many escape-games, many immersions, I target 6 hours of game.

**Every robots created in the game are made from real-world components (arduino, sensors..).** Once you leave the room, you unlock links that allow you to physically build what you used in the game (step-by-step guide linked to platforms like Arduino Project Hub to build your creation in real life).

No coding is required, and robot creation is done without wiring, thanks to a drag-and-drop assembly system of electronic modules.

All the learning is integrated in the rooms. You will discover many use cases in electronic that you can build yourself at home.

**Done right, this game could inspire players to enter a thriving field,** offering a valuable path forward at a time when many are anxious about future job security.

(The illustrations that you see are some drafts and will be animated to make it easy to learn things)

**I’m at the very early stages and trying to decide if I should fully commit to building this. What do you think? Any red flags, feature suggestions, or questions about how it works? Let me know in the comments**
